title: The Language of Experts
text:
Specialised vocabulary, or jargon, allows experts in a discipline to communicate with precision. A cardiologist, for instance, refers to 'myocardial infarction' rather than a heart attack, because the technical term leaves no room for ambiguity.

Critics argue that such terminology can exclude outsiders, creating barriers between professionals and the public. Nevertheless, many educators contend that mastering the lexicon of a field is an essential step toward participating in its debates.

questions.text: According to the passage, why do cardiologists use the term 'myocardial infarction'?
options: Because it leaves no room for ambiguity
Because it is shorter than other words
Because it is older than other terms

questions.text: What do critics say specialised terminology can do?
What can be inferred about the author's view of jargon?
options: It has both benefits and drawbacks
It is useful only for doctors
It is mainly a source of confusion

questions.text: Why might educators consider learning a field's lexicon important?
options: It enables participation in the field's debates
It replaces the need for research

vocabulary.definition: the quality of being exact and accurate
the possibility of being understood in more than one way
things that prevent people from getting or doing something
the set of words used in a particular field or language

paragraph_translations: Specjalistyczne słownictwo, czyli żargon, pozwala ekspertom danej dziedziny komunikować się z precyzją. Na przykład kardiolog mówi 'myocardial infarction' zamiast 'heart attack', ponieważ termin techniczny nie pozostawia miejsca na dwuznaczność.

Krytycy twierdzą, że takie słownictwo może wykluczać osoby z zewnątrz i tworzyć bariery między specjalistami a społeczeństwem. Mimo to wielu pedagogów uważa, że opanowanie leksykonu danej dziedziny jest istotnym krokiem do uczestniczenia w jej dyskusjach.
